title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage with designed, built and proved
when: Runs `lathe check` on the broken-tests fixture.
then: Expects the Errors section, then Warnings, then Coverage, with `[test-file-missing-id] EX-LEND-INV01-T:` among the errors and `[technical-file-missing] EX-LEND-DS01-SV:` among the warnings.

title: The check exits 1 on any error and 0 otherwise, whatever the warnings
when: Runs `lathe check` on the broken-tests fixture and on the clean fixture.
then: Expects status 1 for the broken fixture, and status 0 with `0 errors, 0 warnings.` for the clean one.

title: With --json the check prints each product's whole workspace
when: Runs `lathe check --json`.
then: Expects its output to parse to one product, the root `.`, with the same `Workspace` that `loadWorkspace` returns.

title: Data the store refuses loads no records, and each refusal is a data-refused error
when: Loads a product whose command names an aggregate that does not exist.
then: Expects no records loaded and every problem a data-refused error, naming the missing aggregate.

title: A link from a record of one product to a record of another is refused, whatever the relation; an ID in text is not a link
when: Adds a second product `NX` with a view `NX-V01`, and points the data file's `presents` link at `NX-V01`.
then: Expects one `data-refused` error whose message says `EX-LEND-UC02-FL01-S01 is in product EX`.

title: Data the store refuses is an error naming the file and line, not a crash
when: Runs lathe check on a product whose data/product.jsonl gives a column the table lacks.
then: Expects exit status 1 and a data-refused error naming data/product.jsonl:1.

title: Every problem names its check and, when it has one, its record
when: Loads the complete product with every `presents` link removed, its specification tests not automated yet, one test's file silent and one source file missing, so that more than three checks report problems.
then: Expects every problem in every fixture to name its check in lower case with hyphens, to end as a sentence, and to name its record, whose ID its message contains.

title: A test at a level its kind does not allow is a warning
when: Loads the complete product with its constraint tests and flow test `EX-LEND-UC01-FL01-T` at `service`, then with its constraint tests at `integration`. Loads the complete product with its pattern rule test at each level.
then: Expects one `test-level-not-allowed` warning each, the flow test's saying to run it at system, browser and the constraint test's at unit, integration; and none at `integration`. Expects no test-level-not-allowed warning at any of them.

title: A test run at a level its kind does not allow is a warning; one its kind allows is not
when: With a complete product, runs a constraint test at browser, then at integration.
then: A warning listing the allowed levels; none at integration.

title: A new check needs only a new check row
when: Adds a check row `every-loan-command` to the complete product, reporting each command of the Loan aggregate, with no change to the engine.
then: Expects exactly two `every-loan-command` warnings, for `EX-LEND-CMD01` and `EX-LEND-CMD03`, each saying 'Command <id> changes a loan.'.

title: Checks can read every typed table, with file facts already computed
when: Runs a check that counts the record registry, the links, the test table and the meta-model tables, and reads the file facts.
then: Expects the counts to match the workspace, and each file fact (the file exists, the test's file names its ID) to match the fixture.

title: A check reads the maxChildren setting from the product_setting table
when: Loads a product whose own check reads its `product_setting` row.
then: Expects the check to see `max_children` 3.

title: The record_group view covers a product kind's group_name and a flow step's path
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and adds records of it, grouped and ungrouped.
then: Expects record_group to give the grouped record its group as written, leave out the ungrouped one, and give a flow step its path.

title: Every check runs, in position order, even after one fails
when: Runs three check rows, the second of which reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects their problems in position order, with the failing check reported as one error saying it could not run.

title: A product check runs after Lathe's checks, against the same tables
when: Loads the complete product with its own check `every-event-heard`, which reads the domain_event and hears tables.
then: Expects one `every-event-heard` warning for `EX-LEND-EV02`: 'Domain event EX-LEND-EV02 is heard by no policy.'.

title: A product check reports only on its own product's records, and on none
when: Loads two products, where one has a check that returns every domain and one row with no record.
then: Expects its problems for its own product's domain and for no record, and none for the other product's domain.

title: Without check rows of its own only Lathe's checks run
when: Loads the complete product with its own checks and `src/dates.ts` missing, and sets aside its own checks' problems.
then: Expects every other problem to come from one of Lathe's checks: `technical-file-missing` and `not-built`.

title: A product check's name comes from its row, not from a check column its query returns
when: Loads the product check `every-event-heard`, whose query returns `house-rule` in a check column.
then: Expects no problem under `house-rule`.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused by the store, so it never runs
when: Writes a product check named `view-unused`, like one of Lathe's, into the product's `data/check.jsonl` and loads it.
then: Expects one `data-refused` error saying `check view-unused is already on lathe/data/check.jsonl`.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
when: Loads a product whose check `broken` reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects one error with no record under `broken`, saying the check could not run.

title: A product names no checks folder: lathe.config.json refuses a checks setting, since checks are rows
when: Loads a product whose `lathe.config.json` names a `checks` folder.
then: Expects the load to stop with `unknown setting "checks"`.

title: A record with more children of one kind than maxChildren is a warning naming the parent, kind and count
when: With `max_children` 3, gives use case `EX-LEND-UC01` four UC requirements.
then: Expects one `too-many-children` warning on `EX-LEND-UC01` saying 'Use case EX-LEND-UC01 has 4 children of kind uc_requirement, more than the 3'.

title: A record's tests are never counted, however many it holds
when: Adds 20 use case tests under one UC requirement of the complete product.
then: Expects no `too-many-children` warning under the default limit.

title: Too many children and a lone child are warnings, never errors
when: Loads the fixtures that break `too-many-children` and `lone-child` and reads the severity of every problem they report.
then: Expects every `too-many-children` and `lone-child` problem to be a warning, and no errors in either fixture.

title: Without the setting, maxChildren is 15
when: With no `product_setting` row, gives use case `EX-LEND-UC01` sixteen UC requirements.
then: Expects one `too-many-children` warning saying it has 16 children of kind uc_requirement, more than the 15.

title: maxChildren is read from the product's product_setting row, max_children
when: Loads a product whose `product_setting` row gives `max_children` 3.
then: Expects `too-many-children` on the three records over 3, each message naming the product's max_children setting.

title: A capability with exactly one child is a warning naming the child
when: Moves one of the complete product's two use cases into a new capability, leaving each capability with one use case.
then: Expects two `lone-child` warnings, one per capability, each naming its one use case: 'Capability EX-LEND-CAP01 has only one use case, EX-LEND-UC01; merge it into a neighboring capability, or give it more.' and the same for `EX-LEND-CAP02` and `EX-LEND-UC02`.

title: A lone child counts the capability's own children of every kind
when: Loads capabilities with one use case that has two requirements, with a use case and a record of a product kind, and with nothing.
then: Expects lone-child on the capabilities with one use case only, and none once each has a second child of another kind or has none.

title: A flow's steps are counted per path
when: Loads a flow with three steps on its main path and three on refused under a limit of 3, then four on refused.
then: Expects no warning, then one naming the refused path.

title: too-many-children counts grouped requirements per group, groups compared in any case
when: With `max_children` 2, gives a use case three requirements in the group Limits (one written `limits ` in lower case with a trailing space) and one in Other, beside its ungrouped one.
then: Expects one `too-many-children` warning, saying it has 3 children of kind uc_requirement in group Limits.

title: too-many-children counts a product kind's records per group_name
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and puts seven of its records under one domain, in two groups of two and one of three, under a limit of 2; then only the two groups of two.
then: Expects one warning, naming the group of three; with only the groups of two, four records under the domain, none.

title: A group with one member is a lone-child warning on its parent, standard rules included
when: Puts every standard rule of the complete product in the group `Imports`, and its API requirements, with one more added, in the group `Errors`, written once as ` errors`.
then: Expects one `lone-child` warning: 'Standard EX-STD-CODE's group "Imports" has only one standard rule, EX-STD-CODE-R01; merge it into a neighboring group, or give it more.', and none for the Errors group, whose two members match in any case.

title: A product kind's group with one member is a lone-child warning
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and puts three of its records under one domain, two in one group and one alone in another.
then: Expects one lone-child warning, naming the group of one and its member.

title: An aggregate with more entities than the limit is a warning naming it, the count and the limit
when: With `max_entities_per_aggregate` 3.
then: Expects no warning for an aggregate with 3 entities, and an `aggregate-too-large` warning for one with 4, naming it, the count and the limit and saying to split it.

title: Without the setting the entities limit is 7
when: With no `product_setting` row.
then: Expects no warning for an aggregate with 7 entities, and a warning for one with 8.

title: Every problem of a product shows in one place, as the data is after its latest change
when: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, the Owner opens the product's Checks page and a data file gains an unused view while it is open.
then: The page counts the product's errors and warnings, and counts the new error without a reload.

title: A product's problems read lists its own by check, errors first, then the workspace's, counted, and leaves out every other product's
when: Reads list-problems over two products with a run of the checks whose problems are about each product's records, about no record and about an ID no record has; then without a run; then through the CLI, the MCP tool and HTTP over a run of the checks.
then: Expects each product's own problems by check, errors first, the workspace's for both, the counts, a refusal without a run, and the same answer from the CLI and HTTP.

title: The guard hook refuses an edit of a data file and points at the tools
when: Runs the guard hook on an Edit of `data/product.jsonl`, and on a Write of a relative path in a data folder that `lathe.config.json` names.
then: Expects the permission decision deny, with a reason saying the file is Lathe data to change only with Lathe's MCP tools.

title: The guard hook lets every other edit through, silently
when: Runs the guard hook on a source file, a `.jsonl` file outside the data folder, a data folder outside any Lathe repo, and empty input.
then: Expects exit status 0 and no output each time.

title: The plugin declares the MCP server and the guard hook, and every script they name exists
when: Reads the plugin's `.mcp.json` and `hooks/hooks.json`.
then: Expects the lathe MCP server and one PreToolUse hook, naming `scripts/mcp-server.mjs` and `scripts/guard-data-files.mjs`, both of which exist.

title: A write that adds an essential record, or changes its title or lead, naming technology its kind's group has no business with is refused with the word; one that leaves its text as it was is not
when: On the complete product, changes a use case's goal to click, adds a UC requirement naming the Web app, renames a term Loan row, has a flow step name the Web app and then do so as that interface's variant, has a step click, has a view read from the database, then adds a term Table, a use case naming a table, a second domain with a term Column and a requirement naming a column and then a database, and a pattern rule naming JSON over HTTP, lists Postgres and Table as the product's technology words and writes a use case's actors alone.
then: Expects each leak refused as essential-names-technology with its record and word, the variant step, the view's page, buttons and rows, the term Table and the pattern rule let through until Table is a technology word, and the write that leaves the text as it was let through.

title: The write refusal and accidental-in-essential read one list: every record the check reports is refused when the text it names the word in is written again
when: Loads the complete product with a use case, a UC requirement, a view, a term, an integration and a domain service each naming technology, then writes again, for each, the text the check names the word in.
then: Expects the check to report exactly those records, and each write refused for its record with the word the check named.

title: A change is refused only for the text it sets: a record whose title names technology can still have its lead text changed
when: Loads the complete product with a use case whose title names one of the product's technology words, then changes its goal, then its title to another text with the word, then adds a use case whose goal alone names the word.
then: Expects the change of the goal let through while the check still warns of the title, the change of the title refused for the title alone, and the add refused for its goal.

title: A write that links an essential record to an accidental one, or declares a relation that would, is refused; an outcome may still be measured by a record of an accidental kind
when: Gives the complete product an essential kind of its own with a relation to any record, declares that relation to a table, adds a record of the kind citing a table and then a use case, and declares measured_by from the outcome to a report kind.
then: Expects the declaration and the link to the table refused as essential-links-accidental naming both ends, and the link to the use case and the measured_by declaration let through.

title: A product's essential records are listed alone, by domain, with their kind, title and lead text
when: Lists the complete product's essential records, as the query and its text, then asks for a product there is not.
then: Expects the Lending domain's essential records in ID order and those in no domain last, with no technical record, pattern, slot or test, the count and text to match, and the unknown product refused.

title: The check-and-fix skill has the Agent hold each essential record to the domain-expert test before proposing a change
when: Reads the plugin's check-and-fix skill.
then: Expects it to run the essential review's list, ask the domain-expert question of each record, list what fails with why for the Owner, and change no essential record on that alone.

title: The Reader finds a record in a domain
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a domain's page, finds a record in it by its ID and then by its title, and opens it.
then: The domain's page lists its records by stage and kind; quick find (Cmd/Ctrl+K) finds the record by its ID and by words of its title, and choosing it opens the record's page.

title: The Reader follows a record's links
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: From a record's page, follows a link out and a link in to the records at their ends, then goes back.
then: Each link under Links out and Links in opens the record at its other end, and Back returns to the first record's page where it was left.

title: The record summaries read places each record of a product's space and gives its file, line, digest and the links among them
when: Reads list-record-summaries for one of two products, with a value object one domain uses and then two, a link, and a part row changed.
then: Expects each record placed up its parents, by its ID or in the one domain that uses it, nothing of the other product, no column beyond its summary, the links among them, and a digest that changes only when its rows do.

title: The space's record index holds each record's summary with its children and its links both ways
when: Builds a space's record index from the summaries and meta model reads over the served data.
then: Expects each record with its parent, product and domain, its data file and line and no other column, and each link both ways.

title: The Reader walks the model as a graph
when: In each layout of the graph, clicks a labeled box in view.
then: Expects the address to change to the clicked box's page, that box drawn as the focus, the header strip's breadcrumb shown and, for a record, `.header-strip-id` showing its ID.

title: The Reader walks the graph through the nav's groups
when: Opens Lathe's graph and clicks the boxes of `LA-EXP`, its Use cases stage, a capability and a use case in turn.
then: Expects each click to move the address to the box's page and draw it as the focus, with nothing outside the graph's boxes moving.

title: The Reader reads a record as wiki, graph or model
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a record at its address and reads it in the wiki card, then switches the stage behind it to the Graph, the ERD and the Trace, with the mouse and from the keyboard.
then: The record opens at `/<id>` with its page in the wiki card; the Graph, ERD and Trace buttons of the stage switch, and Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2 and Ctrl+3, change only the stage behind the card, the address keeping `?stage=`, and the card shows the same record throughout.

title: The Reader reads a flow step by step
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a flow's page and reads each path's steps in order, with what each invokes, where it happens and what it fulfills.
then: Each path lists its steps in order, and each step shows the command or query it invokes, the view it happens in and the requirements it fulfills, each a link to its record.

title: The Reader moves between products as spaces
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a page in one product, switches to another product's space from the rail, then back.
then: The other product's space shows only its own records, problems and counts; switching back opens the first product on the page last visited in it.

title: The rail shows with two products and not with one
when: Opens Lathe's workspace of two products in Chromium, then the same with its own product alone.
then: Expects the rail with both spaces; with one product no rail, the product's name and icon at the top of the nav.

title: The Reader reads a product in its stage folders
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a product and unfolds Shared and each domain's five stages in the nav.
then: Shared lists what the product shares, and each domain unfolds into its five stages, Domain model, Use cases, Interface design, Technical specification and Test plan, each holding one folder per kind with its records.

title: The folder tree read gives Shared and each domain its stages, a folder per kind and what folds under each record
when: Reads get-folder-tree for one of two products, with terms one of which builds on another.
then: Expects Shared and the product's domain only, an aggregate's entity and invariant folded under it, terms bottom-up, a stage's one folder shown directly, and the product's pattern with its rule under Shared.

title: The Reader reads the technical specification and test plan by kind
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a domain's Technical specification and Test plan in the nav, on the domain page and in the graph.
then: The domain's technical records and tests appear grouped by kind, the same kinds in the same order, in the nav's Technical specification and Test plan, on the domain page and as the graph's groups.

title: The Reader explores several places at once in tabs
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens several records in tabs, changes each one's stage and scroll, and reloads the page.
then: After the reload the same tabs are open with the same one active, and each comes back on its own page, stage and scroll.

title: The Reader reads a domain's ERD
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a domain on the ERD stage, then one of its aggregates.
then: The ERD draws the domain's aggregates with their entities, fields and the links between them; opening an aggregate draws that aggregate's own entities and fields.

title: The ERD read gives a product's domains, aggregates with their entities (root first) and fields, and its lines, nothing of another product
when: Reads get-erd for one of two products, with a has-one link and a field typed by another aggregate.
then: Expects each box with its parent, root and empty marks, each entity's fields with their types, a has-one line and a reference line to the other aggregate's root, and a refusal for a product that is not there.

title: The Reader reads a record's history in the wiki card
when: Makes the suite's data a git repository with twenty-two commits that touch a domain and one change not committed, opens the domain's graph, shows its history in the wiki card, opens a commit and loads more.
then: Expects the history to show the change not committed and `Retitle 21`, opening `Retitle 20` to show `Exploring 20`, and Load more to reach the first commit, `The data`.

title: The Reader reads a domain's endpoints and integrations
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a command or a query to find its endpoint, and an integration to find the steps that exchange with it.
then: The command's or query's page links to the endpoint that exposes it, and the integration's page lists the flow steps that exchange with it, each a link to its record.

title: The record diff finds records added, removed and changed field by field, with their part rows and links
when: In one store write, retitles a use case and gives it a goal, an actor and a link, removes another use case and adds a third; then diffs the rows before and after.
then: Expects the three records changed, removed and added in ID order; the changed one's title and goal before and after, its actor added and its link added; the added and removed ones with no rows listed; nothing for the same rows; the reverse diff undoing it; and a base plus its delta giving the rows back.

title: The record changes read lists each record added, removed and changed since the baseline, per product
when: Reads list-record-changes for a product with a baseline, and with none.
then: Expects each record that differs with its change and nothing of another product, and with no baseline the reason and no change.

title: The Record changes read over HTTP compares with the baseline its since names, read from git
when: Reads GET /api/record-changes/list-record-changes for a product in a temporary git repo since the last commit, since the branch left main and since a noted commit, then in a folder with no git, at a commit that does not exist, with a since that is no baseline, with no product and for an unknown product.
then: Expects the records changed since each baseline with their fields before and after; no baseline and no change, with the reason, with no git or no such commit; 400 for a bad since or no product; 422 for an unknown product.

title: Every stage marks the records a reload added, changed and removed, with dots only under reduced motion
when: Opens an aggregate's graph at depth 3 and reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, then with the added one gone, then with the renamed one gone.
then: Expects the renamed command marked changed and the new one added, the command added and then removed gone with no ghost, and a ghost where the removed command was.

title: Highlight changes dims the unchanged records against each baseline, and since I last looked moves when it is turned off or the product left
when: Reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, turns Highlight changes on, picks since the branch left main, then since I last looked, and turns it off.
then: Expects a count of 2, the changed command at full strength and every unchanged box dimmed to a fifth, the new command's box carrying the New pill and the renamed one's the Changed pill, the branch baseline asked for and kept in the session setting, the last look kept at the last commit with the same 2 changes, and turning it off moving the last look to now with a count of 0 and both commands in its delta.

title: A record removed that the baseline had leaves only its ghost, and one new since the baseline then removed leaves nothing
when: Opens the page with a command already added since the baseline, turns Highlight changes on, removes it, then removes a command the baseline had.
then: Expects the added one gone with no box and no ghost, and the baseline one gone with its ghost and no box.

title: A changed record's wiki card shows its changes, and an added one says New since its baseline
when: Opens a command's page, reloads the data with the command renamed and a new one added, then goes to the new command.
then: Expects the wiki card's Changes section to say Changed since the last commit with the old title struck out and the new one inserted, and the new command's card to say New since the last commit.

title: The wiki card lists the links a changed record gained and lost, beside each field old → new
when: Opens a command's page, reloads the data with the command retitled and redescribed, one event it raises replaced by another.
then: Expects the Changes section to list the title and the description each old → new, and the links "Added raises" the new event and "Removed raises" the old one.

title: Follow glides to each change as it lands and turns off, with a note, when the Reader moves the camera or focuses
when: Turns Follow on from an aggregate's graph and reloads the data with a command renamed, scrolls the wheel on the stage, then turns Follow on again and moves the address to the aggregate.
then: Expects the focus to follow to the renamed command with Follow still on, then Follow off with the note that you moved the camera, and off again with the note that you moved the focus.

title: The Changes panel lists the changes newest first by record, a click focuses one, and its toggle counts them
when: Reloads the data twice, renaming a command and then an aggregate, opens the Changes panel from its toggle and clicks the command's card.
then: Expects the toggle to count 2, the aggregate's card before the command's, and the click to focus the command with the panel still open.

title: Roll-ups count the new, changed and removed records under each container, and the nav shows them beside each folder
when: Counts the changes under each place of a small tree with a record added, one changed and one removed, writes the roll-up text, and counts the same changes for the nav's folders and domains.
then: Expects each container to count only the changes strictly under it, the text "1 new · 2 changed · 1 removed" leaving out zeros, a removed record counted under the nearest container its ID names, and the nav's counts by folder and domain the same.

title: With Highlight changes on, the Graph's boxes carry their pill and each container its roll-up, and the nav shows the counts
when: Reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, turns Highlight changes on at depth 3, and reads the Graph's scene and the nav.
then: Expects the new command's box to carry the New pill and the renamed one the Changed pill, their entity's box the roll-up "1 new · 1 changed", and the nav to show the counts beside the domain.

title: The edge hints count the changed boxes past each edge
when: Counts the changed boxes of a map past each edge of a canvas, with some inside it, some left of it and some below it.
then: Expects only the boxes whose centers lie outside counted, on the side they lie, and none for an edge with nothing past it.

title: Next change and Previous change step through the changed records in ID order, around at the ends
when: Steps forward and back through a walk of changed records from a changed focus, from an unchanged one, past each end, and through an empty walk.
then: Expects the next record after the focus (or the first), the previous one before it (or the last), numbers compared by value, and nothing for an empty walk.

title: The ] and [ keys move the focus to the next and previous changed record and announce it
when: Reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, then presses ] twice and [ once from an aggregate.
then: Expects the focus on the renamed command, then the added one, then back on the renamed one, each announced with its place in the walk.

title: The Reader reads a journey step by step, and where the acting role changes
when: Opens a journey's page with a main path of a use case, a handoff and a use case of another actor, and an alternate path.
then: Expects the main path first in order, then the alternate, each step with what it carries out, its actors (the product for the handoff) and its capability and domain.

title: A use case names the journeys it is a step of, with the steps before and after it
when: Opens the page of a use case that is step 1 of one journey and step 3 of another, then a policy that is a handoff.
then: Expects each journey with its step, path and position and the next and previous steps, each a link; none on a use case in no journey.

title: In the graph a journey's steps sit under it, in order on each path
when: Frames a journey on the Map with a step moved from last to first.
then: Expects its steps nested in it in path and position order, not ID order, with a then arrow between consecutive steps and a line from each to what it carries out.

title: The layout and the minimap chosen in the graph hold on another page and after a reload
when: In the graph of a use case, turns the minimap on and chooses the Nested layout, opens another record's graph, then opens the app again.
then: Expects the minimap on and the Nested layout on the other record's graph and after the reload, and the session settings to hold both.

title: A view or an integration has no owner and takes its product from its ID, and one nothing uses is an error
when: Every presents link from a view and every exchange of a step with an integration is removed; a view's ID names no product.
then: view-unused and integration-unused errors; the ID refused by id-prefix.

title: A view, integration, value object, specification or UI component that nothing uses is an error, each named
when: With a complete product that has no unused errors, removes every link and field type that uses its views, integrations, value objects, specifications and UI components.
then: Each of the five unused checks gives one error on its record.

title: A view, which has no owner, cannot be moved under a parent
when: Moves a view, which has no owner, under the product.
then: Expects a `command` refusal saying a view has no parent, so it cannot move.

title: A rule of the interface design is a view requirement under its view or an API requirement under its endpoint

title: An endpoint sits under the one command or query it exposes, and a step reaches it only through that command or query
when: An endpoint has no parent, or two; a step invokes an endpoint.

title: A rule of an endpoint is an API requirement under it
when: A product is loaded.
then: The interface design's only obligations are view and API requirements, under their view or endpoint, counted in coverage.

title: An integration has no owner and takes its product from its ID, and one no step or policy exchanges with is an error

then: view-unused and integration-unused errors; the ID refused by id-prefix.

title: A UI component that renders no view is an error
when: Removes what uses each record of the complete product, one at a time.
then: Expects an error naming the record, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: The reference says a domain is one business capability, and the domain-named-for-technology check calls it a vertical slice whose technology is its technical records

title: The modeling skill's first step finds the business capabilities and makes each a slice, with the questions that tell one from a layer

then: Expects its first section to find the business capabilities before any record is written, and to ask at least four questions that tell a capability from a layer.

title: Each domain says its subdomain type: core, supporting or generic
when: A domain is written with no subdomain type, and with one that is not core, supporting or generic.
then: The column is required and described; both rows are refused.

title: A capability sits under a domain with a required whole-number position, and every use case sits under one of its domain's capabilities

title: A repository persists exactly one aggregate, and an aggregate no repository persists is a gap

then: Expects an aggregate-without-repository gap for the unpersisted aggregate only, and no other problem.

title: Each Domain command changes one domain through its repository, held to its rules
when: Builds a domain with its own commands, changes its records and links, removes a domain service and a domain, then changes a repository to persist an aggregate another repository persists and adds a second repository persisting it, and runs domain commands from the CLI, the MCP tools and HTTP.

title: A repository that persists no aggregate is an error until its link is written

then: Expects one `repository-persists-nothing` error naming that repository, and its aggregate an aggregate-without-repository gap.

title: A domain's services, which its commands and queries call, and its terms sit under the domain
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Expects a read model under its domain with `read_model_field` parts and `reads` to an aggregate, a query under its read model, a domain service and a term under their domain (a term requiring `meaning`), `calls` from a command, a query or a read model to a domain service, each described in the reference in the domain-model stage, and the example's `EX-LEND-RM01` reads `EX-LEND-A2`, `EX-LEND-CMD01` calls `EX-LEND-DS01` and `EX-LEND-QRY01` sits under `EX-LEND-RM01`.

title: A capability serves any number of outcomes, and an outcome is served by any number of capabilities, of its own product
when: Links two capabilities to two outcomes every way, a use case to an outcome, and a capability to another product's outcome.
then: The links load; the use case's link is refused by its foreign key, and the other product's by link-crosses-product.

title: Each record moved to another domain takes its IDs, with everything under it, and nothing names an old ID
when: Moves an aggregate, a capability, a term, a repository, a read model, a specification, a test data set, a tooling record and a shared module to a second domain, then moves one to a domain of another product and one to an ID that is taken.
then: Expects each record and every record under it to take the new domain's ID, every link, field and text that named an old ID to name the new one, the data to load with no problem, and the last two moves refused, changing nothing.

title: A product page lists its domains by position, and Change a domain reorders them
when: Adds a second domain whose ID sorts first at the next position, reads the product page, then changes the first domain's position past it and reads again.
then: Expects the domains in position order, not ID order, and the other order after the change.

title: The space's domains, its folder tree and the Map's districts follow the positions
when: Builds the model fixture's index, then again with the positions of its two domains swapped.
then: Expects the index's domains, the folder tree's and the Map's districts in position order each time.

title: An entity sits under an aggregate and needs a role, a value object has no owner, and entities link to entities by has_one and has_many
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: An entity sits under an aggregate with a required role, a value object has no owner and its constraints sit under it, the four field tables are parts, and has_one and has_many join entities, all described.

title: A well-formed domain model gives no entity problem, and each entity rule fails on its own data
when: With a well-formed domain model, leaves a child unreached, links across aggregates, adds a second root, drops a role and links an entity to itself.
then: No problems on the good model; entity-unreferenced, has-crosses-aggregate and refusals for the rest.

title: An entity has its fields in order, each with a name, a meaning, exactly one type and whether it is required
when: Reads the complete product's entity, and gives a field no type or two.
then: Its fields come in order, each with its name, meaning, one type and whether it is required; a field with no type or two is refused.

title: An entity, event or read model with no fields is a coverage gap
when: Loads an entity, an event and a read model with no fields.
then: Each is a coverage gap.

title: Another aggregate is referenced by a field typed by it: a foreign key in its own domain, a plain ID from another domain
when: With an entity whose field is typed by another domain's aggregate, adds foreign keys within the domain and into the other domain.
then: The field and the same-domain key load; the cross-domain key is refused; a has_many into another aggregate is an error.

title: Uniqueness is an invariant that a unique key may name and back up, built only by its rule, and only a unique key may name one
when: With an invariant a unique key names, whose rule's file is missing, then present; then a primary key and an index naming the invariant.
then: The invariant is not built through the key, then built through its rule; a primary key or index naming an invariant is refused.

title: A child entity its root does not reach by has_one or has_many is a warning
when: Removes every `has_one` link of the complete product, leaving a child entity its root does not reach.
then: Expects one `entity-unreferenced` warning, on that child.

title: A domain event sits under an aggregate, a command under the entity it changes raises and checks, and a policy under a command hears one event
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Events, commands with raises and checks, and policies hearing one event and exchanging with integrations are in the schema and described.

title: A command changes only its own aggregate, the one of the entity it sits under, and the schema keeps no way to record another
when: Loads commands under entities of their aggregates, and reads the schema's tables.
then: Each command counts for the aggregate of the entity it sits under, and no table records another aggregate a command changes.

title: A policy names the integrations it exchanges with
when: Adds an integration to the Open a loan command's data set, changes its policy to exchange with it, adds a second policy that does, and names an integration that is not there.
then: Expects only the exchanges_with link written, the command read with the policy's integrations, and the missing integration refused.

title: Constraints sit under a value object, invariants under an aggregate, specifications have no owner and read one domain's aggregates, and policies sit under their command, each with a statement
when: A specification reads another domain's aggregate, and an invariant has no statement.
then: Expects a constraint under its value object, an invariant under its aggregate, a policy under its command and a specification with no owner, scoped by domain, each an obligation requiring a statement; `reads` from a specification to an aggregate scoped to its domain; the reading of another domain's aggregate refused by `link-scope`; and the bare invariant refused with 'invariant.statement is required'.

title: A specification no command checks and no query selects by is an error
when: Removes what uses each record of the complete product, one at a time.
then: Expects an error naming the record, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: Read models with their fields and reads, queries of one read model, domain services that commands and queries call, and terms are in the schema
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Expects a read model under its domain with `read_model_field` parts and `reads` to an aggregate, a query under its read model, a domain service and a term under their domain (a term requiring `meaning`), `calls` from a command, a query or a read model to a domain service, each described in the reference in the domain-model stage, and the example's `EX-LEND-RM01` reads `EX-LEND-A2`, `EX-LEND-CMD01` calls `EX-LEND-DS01` and `EX-LEND-QRY01` sits under `EX-LEND-RM01`.

title: A value object has no owner, its fields are its own rows, and its constraints sit under it
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: An entity sits under an aggregate with a required role, a value object has no owner and its constraints sit under it, the four field tables are parts, and has_one and has_many join entities, all described.

title: A record that nothing uses is an error
when: Loads the complete product with no presents, exchanges_with, checks, renders or starts_from links, and no field typed by its value object.
then: Expects one error each for the view, the integration, the value object, the specification, the test data set and the UI component, saying what uses such a record and to link it or remove it.

title: A value object used by a read model is used, and a query selecting by a specification uses it
when: Loads a value object typed only by a read model field and a specification only a query selects by.
then: Expects no unused error for either.

title: A domain event sits under its aggregate and says whether it is published
when: The schema and the reference are read.
then: Events, commands with raises and checks, and policies hearing one event are in the schema and described.

title: A domain event's fields are its event_field rows in position order, as an entity's are
when: Loads event fields written out of position order.
then: The fields come back in position order, only on events, in an entity field's shape.

title: A domain event with no fields is a gap, and a field without a name, or named twice, is refused
when: An event loses its fields; a field is blank, unnamed or named twice.
then: The event is a gap; the three fields are refused.

title: An event a policy hears is delivered by outbox
when: Loads the complete product with the event a policy hears delivered in process, with no event type, or with an event type that gives no delivery; then with that event's aggregate in no table, or kept in browser storage, a file or memory.
then: Expects an `event-not-by-outbox` problem naming the event, its policy and the fix in each of the first three cases, none for a published event that only feeds a read model, and none when the aggregate is kept outside a database.

title: A storage requirement is counted in its domain, built only through what stores it, and proved by its test
when: Loads the complete product, then removes its repository's data store, its repository's file or its test, and adds a requirement under a read model.
then: Expects the requirement designed, built and proved in its domain; not built without the data store or the file, not proved without its test; and one under a read model built through its reader.

title: loadWorkspace returns the Workspace contract
when: Loads a fixture.
then: Expects exactly the fields of `Workspace` and its parts in `lathe/src/types.ts`, including the built coverage counts, as plain JSON.

title: Loading Lathe's spec takes under 2 s and a live reload under 500 ms
when: `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf`. Loads a copy of Lathe's data cold, then changes one row through the store and reloads.
then: Expects the median cold load under 2 s and the median load after the change under 500 ms; measures the reference without a budget. On a busy machine (a one-minute load average above 12) it judges nothing and exits 3.

title: A reload after a write times each phase and gives what a fresh load gives
when: Loads a copy of a fixture twice, changes a use case's title through the store and loads again twice.
then: Expects every phase timed (open, files, checks, coverage, total), the same workspace when nothing changed, the new title after the write, and a further load equal to that one.

title: Each load reads the files afresh and writes nothing
when: Loads a copy of a fixture, changes a use case's title through the store, and loads again.
then: Expects the second load to show the change, the first result untouched, and the folder to hold no new files after either load.

title: Each load reads changed data afresh, and the reference is kept only until a data file changes
when: Builds the reference of a copy of a fixture twice, declares a product kind `memo` through the store and builds it again.
then: Expects the same reference object the second time, and a new one holding the `memo` kind after the data file changed.

title: A cold lathe use-case get-use-case takes under 800 ms
when: `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf`. Runs `lathe use-case get-use-case --id LA-PLT-UC01` on a copy of Lathe's repo in a fresh process once to fill the schema cache, then five times more.
then: Expects the median, from the process's start to its exit, under 800 ms. On a busy machine (a one-minute load average above 12) it judges nothing and exits 3.

title: A cached schema gives what one built afresh gives, and is used without being built again
when: Loads the fixture with no cache, then twice with an empty cache folder. Changes a migration's text, and, separately, stamps each cache file with another key and an altered schema. Overwrites Lathe's cache file with garbage, then with its first third, then the product's file with garbage, loading after each. Starts two processes at once on the fixture with an empty cache folder.
then: Expects the same schema, placements, parents and tables each time (no trace of the cache's stamp), one file for Lathe's schema and one for the fixture's kinds, and the second load to leave both files as they were. Expects a changed migration to change the key, and the next load to give what a fresh build gives, replace both files and remove an older base schema's file; the load after uses the files as they are. Expects each load to give what a fresh build gives, and the file to be whole again after it. Expects both to print what a fresh build gives, the folder to hold the two cache files and nothing half-written, and a load after to use them as they are.

title: Files a whole build passed load without building again, answer as the whole build does, and a changed file or bad stamp is built whole
when: Loads the fixture twice on an empty cache folder; adds a domain whose product is not there, puts the file back, then changes a description; overwrites the stamp with garbage, then empties it; runs `lathe use-case get-use-case` twice in fresh processes, then again after adding a use case of no capability.
then: Expects the second load not to build whole and to give the same schema, rows, record, origin and record_scope as the first, with one stamp; the broken file to be refused exactly as an uncached load refuses it, and never stamped; the file put back to load from its old stamp; the passing change to be built whole once and then stamped; each bad stamp to be built whole and written again with its key; and the cached CLI run to print exactly what the first did, and the refused one to fail exactly as an uncached run fails.

title: Init writes a config and a first product record through the store, and refuses bad or repeated input
when: Runs `lathe init` in a new folder, again in the same folder, with bad or missing options, and in a folder whose config names another data folder.
then: Expects `lathe.config.json` with `{ "schema": <this Lathe's schema version>, "data": "data" }` and the product's row in `data/product.jsonl` that passes `lathe check`; a second init refused with exit 2 and the row unchanged; an invalid or missing prefix or name refused with nothing written; and an existing config kept, with the product written to its data folder.

title: A product's lathe.config.json chooses the data folder
when: Reads a lathe.config.json whose data setting names spec-data.
then: Expects the data folder to be spec-data under the product root.

title: A config with an unknown setting is refused and names it
when: Writes a `lathe.config.json` naming the unknown setting `diagrams`, then one naming `specs`, `checks` and `metaExtensions`, and loads each with `loadConfig`, the first with `loadWorkspace` too.
then: Expects the config naming `diagrams` refused by `loadConfig` with 'unknown setting "diagrams"' and by `loadWorkspace` naming it, and the one naming the Markdown settings refused with 'unknown settings "specs", "checks", "metaExtensions"'.

title: The store reads the data folder lathe.config.json names
when: Opens a product whose lathe.config.json names another data folder.
then: Expects the records of that folder.

title: A product's own kind is a row of its own data, adding a table for that product only
when: Declares a memo kind as a product_kind row of the complete product.
then: Expects the store to have a memo table for that product, and none for the product without the row.

title: A product declares a kind of its own in any stage and adds its records in the same write
when: Declares a product kind with a field and adds its record in one write, then a bad date, a kind named like one of Lathe's tables and a link of the product's relation between Lathe's kinds.
then: Expects the kind in the schema and its file written, each of the others refused with its rule, and the record there after reopening.

title: Two branches that each added a row merge through git with the driver set up as the README says
when: Reads the package's README.
then: Expects it to give `git config merge.lathe-data.name "Lathe data files"`, `git config merge.lathe-data.driver "npx lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P"` and the `.gitattributes` line `**/data/*.jsonl merge=lathe-data`.

title: The config's tests globs choose the test files; node_modules, dist and another product's folder are never read
when: Loads a product with unnamed test cases in a matching file, in node_modules, in dist and in a folder with its own lathe.config.json, first with the default globs and then with tests naming other globs; then writes tests values that are not lists of globs.
then: Expects test-case-unnamed for the matching file alone, following the globs, and each bad tests value refused naming the key.

title: A workspace loads each listed product from its own folder, and refuses a listing that is wrong
when: Reads a workspace whose config lists a product folder, then configs that list the workspace itself, a folder twice, a folder with no config, a product that lists its own, and the same product ID in two folders.
then: Expects each product loaded from its own folder with its own records and coverage, and each wrong listing refused with a message naming it.

title: lathe check reports each product of the workspace, then them all
when: Runs `lathe check` at a workspace of two products, one with an error.
then: Expects a report per product, each with its own counts, then the counts of both, and exit code 1; with the error fixed, exit code 0.

title: The workspace traces no file of a listed product's folder
when: Loads a workspace whose listed product folder holds source files, tests, a router file and a package.json.
then: Expects none of them among the workspace's source files, test cases, routes or packages, and a package folder listed inside the product refused.

title: The server reads a changed data file's table again and sends spec:changed naming it and the read models that read it
when: Runs the dev API plugin against a stand-in Vite server, reads the meta model, then writes a data file and tells the plugin it changed; then changes a schema file, a file in another folder and README.md.
then: Expects the plugin to watch the product's data folder and Lathe's own data and schema folders; the data file's change sent as `spec:changed` naming its table and the read models reading it, not the meta model; a schema file's change to name every read model; and a file in another folder or README.md to send nothing.

title: Reads the data again when a file changes under it
when: Changes a data file behind the dev API plugin and reads the product's record summaries; then adds a row the schema refuses, reads again, puts the file back and reads again; and asks a server whose engine cannot be loaded.
then: Expects the answer to hold the changed row, then status 500 with an error naming `use_case.jsonl:2`, then 200 once the file is fixed; and 500 with the reason the engine could not be loaded.

title: Each change is announced with its tables and the read models that read them
when: Serves a product, reads its problems and meta model, writes three changes to its question file, then a title the whole build refuses, then puts the file back.
then: Expects each change announced with the question table and the read models that read it (the product's, not the meta model's), the checks' run announced with the checks' read models, and the refusal and the return to served data each announced naming every read model.

title: A reload of only the changed files gives the same state, problems and coverage as a load from scratch
when: Writes 24 random change sets (a record retitled, a row removed or brought back, a key given twice, a line that is not JSON, a title the integrity queries refuse, a file touched) to a product's data files from a fixed seed; after each, reloads one kept store and builds it whole, and loads a second store from scratch.
then: Expects both to hold the same rows on the same lines, refuse with the same problems, answer every read the same (the kept store from the readers it kept) and find the same problems, coverage and chains; and some rounds refused and some served.

title: A reload reads only the changed tables, reruns only the rules that read them and rebuilds only the read models that read them
when: Touches a data file and reloads, then retitles a question in its file and reloads.
then: Expects the touched file to change nothing; the retitle to reload only the question table, rerun the Product aggregate's rules and fewer than all, keep the meta model's reader and make the use case's again; the store's own database to wait for the whole build, which holds the new title.

title: The checks run in the background after a burst of changes, once the reads answer, and are announced when ready
when: Serves a product, reads its problems and meta model, then writes three changes to one data file in a row; then changes the file and keeps reading the meta model for 400 ms; then writes a title the integrity queries refuse, and puts the file back.
then: Expects each change announced at once with its table and the read models reading it (not the meta model), one checks' run announced after the burst and no more; no checks' run while the reads keep coming, and one after they stop; the refused title served until the whole build refuses it, then every read model announced and every read refused naming the file and line, and every read served again once the file is put back.

title: A command's commit refuses what the whole build would, without building the data whole
when: Adds a view through its command, then a second, then tries a view titled as one already is and a capability at position 0, then builds the data whole.
then: Expects the first two writes held without a database of their own (the file written, the rows current, SQL waiting for the whole build); the duplicate title refused by title-unique and the position by its CHECK, as the whole build refuses them; the whole build to hold both views and its database to become the store's own.

title: On the large product an edit is visible under 500 ms, the checks' run is announced within 4 s and a cold load takes under 4 s
when: `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf`. Loads a copy of the large product cold; then serves it with the use case's page, its space's reads and its problems read once, five times retitles a use case through its own store, as an Agent in another process does, and tells the server its file changed; then five times retitles it through its command's route, as the page does.
then: Expects the median cold load under 4 s, the median edit (from the file's change to the reads the change names answered) and the median write (from the request to the same) under 500 ms, and the median checks' run announced within 4 s of the change. On a busy machine (a one-minute load average above 12) it judges nothing and exits 3.

title: Upgrade lists what it could not convert, and stops without raising the schema when the data no longer loads

then: Expects the to-do listed and the schema raised; the refusal listed as a to-do with the schema unchanged; and the missing converter refused with nothing changed.

title: Upgrade refuses a working tree with changes, or no git
when: Upgrades a product with a file not committed, then once it is committed, then a product not under git.
then: Expects the first refused naming the changed file with the schema unchanged, the second upgraded, and the third refused as not in a git repository.

title: The MCP launcher warns once when the installed Lathe is not the major version the skills were written for

then: Expects the manifest's major to be the package's, the warning with both versions and the schema in the first result only, and no warning at the same major version.

title: The launcher says why it cannot start outside a Lathe repo
when: Starts the launcher in a folder with no Lathe repo.
then: Expects it to exit saying why it cannot start.

title: Text with quotes, newlines and backticks given as JSON is written exactly, from stdin or a file, in the tool's shape
when: Adds a requirement from stdin and changes a use case's goal from a file with an aggregate command's `--json`, each with quotes, newlines, backticks, tabs and accents, then a flow step's list as JSON and the same command's tool. Pipes an add under a use case that does not exist as JSON and gives the same add as flags; pipes JSON with a field flag, text that does not parse, and names a JSON file that does not exist.
then: Expects the text read back exactly and the tool and the CLI to read one input one way; the same refusal as the flag form with the data files unchanged; and exit 2 with the reason for bad usage, nothing written.

title: No skill tells the Agent to write spec files by hand
when: Reads every skill of the plugin.
then: Expects no skill to tell the Agent to edit data files, none to name a tool, and each to point to lathe/REFERENCE.md exactly once.

title: The chat runs the Owner's own Claude Code in the folder and continues its session
when: Drives a `ChatSession` against a stand-in CLI: sends a message on a new session; opens a saved session to resume, closes it and sends again; and opens one to fork.
then: Expects the answer streamed and completed, the session named by a UUID and the CLI run in the folder; the resume run with `--resume`, the saved items shown first, and the CLI started again on the same session after it ended; and the fork run with `--resume <id> --fork-session`, ending under a new session ID.

title: The chat runs the CLI headless, with structured input and output
when: Builds the CLI's arguments for a new, a resumed and a forked session, and writes a message, a permission answer and a stop as lines for the CLI.
then: Expects `-p` with stream-json input and output, verbose partial messages and `--permission-prompt-tool stdio`, plus `--resume` and `--fork-session` as asked; a user line with the text; a control response that allows with the tool's input unchanged, or denies; and an interrupt control request.

title: The chat finds the Owner's own claude
when: Looks for `claude` with a configured path, on the PATH and where the installers put it, and reads `claudePath` from the settings.
then: Expects the configured path when it exists and none when it does not; else the first `claude` on the PATH, else `~/.local/bin/claude`, else none; and the setting trimmed, an empty one left out.

title: The chat is offered in the desktop app on a wide window, and nowhere else
when: Opens a use case in a browser, with no desktop bridge, and in the desktop app on a phone-sized screen.
then: Expects no chat panel and no chat toggle in the browser, and no chat panel on the phone.

title: Record IDs in Claude's answers open the record on the stage
when: Pushes a question and an answer naming `DM-SHOP-CMD01` in bold and `NOPE-1` into the chat, then clicks the record's link.
then: Expects the answer drawn as Markdown, `DM-SHOP-CMD01` a link titled with its record's title and `NOPE-1` left as text, and the click opening the command's page on the stage.

title: Tool calls are rows that expand, and a turn's changed records show as diffs
when: Pushes a finished tool call and expands its row; pushes a running turn during which the data reloads with a command renamed, then its answer; and compares two indexes with one record removed, one added and one changed.
then: Expects the row closed until clicked, then its result and a done mark; the turn followed by "1 record changed" with the command's old title struck out and its new one inserted; and the removed, added and changed records found, the changed field with its before and after, and none between an index and itself.

title: The CLI's stream becomes the chat's text, tool rows and prompts
when: Feeds the CLI's stream lines into the chat's state: streamed then completed text, tool calls with their results, a subagent's text, a permission request and its cancel, turn results and unreadable lines; then diffs two states into patches.
then: Expects the text once, completed in place, and the session's ID; each tool call a row with its label and one-line summary, closed by its result or its error; a subagent's text kept out; the prompt pending, then withdrawn; the turn ended idle with an error notice or "Stopped."; unreadable lines ignored; and a patch of only the changed items, a reset when items are gone.

title: A permission prompt waits for the Owner, and Stop ends the turn
when: Asks the stand-in CLI for a tool that needs permission, then allows it, denies it, or stops the turn; and opens a session whose CLI does not exist.
then: Expects the prompt pending with the tool and its summary; once allowed, the answer recorded and the tool done, a second answer refused; once denied, the tool in error; on Stop, the chat stopping, then idle with the prompt withdrawn and "Stopped.", the next message going to the same process; and a CLI that cannot start closing the chat with an error notice.

title: The Owner answers a permission prompt in the chat and stops a turn
when: Pushes a pending permission prompt and answers Allow once, then Deny; sends a message with Enter and stops the turn with the Stop button and with Escape; and walks the messages with the arrow keys, Home and End.
then: Expects the prompt naming the tool and what it would do, each answer sent to the shell and, once answered, "Allowed once" with no buttons; the message sent, "Claude is working…" shown and two stops sent; and focus moving between the messages, only the last in the tab order.

title: The picker lists the folder's saved sessions by title and date, and warns of one open elsewhere
when: Names the session store's folder for a product folder, titles sessions from their transcripts' ends, lists a folder's transcripts with one running elsewhere, reads the registry of running sessions, and finds transcripts by session ID.
then: Expects the folder named as the CLI names it; a title from the custom title, else the summary, else the first real prompt, cut to 80 characters; sessions newest first, empty ones left out, marked running or just written; only other processes' live sessions from the registry; and only a session ID's own transcript found, a path or an unknown ID refused.

title: The picker resumes, forks or starts a session, and warns of one open elsewhere
when: Opens the chat's session picker and resumes, forks and starts sessions; picks a session open in another client; opens the picker with no Claude Code found; and dates sessions.
then: Expects the sessions by title and age, the busy one marked "Open elsewhere"; resume, fork and new sent to the shell; for the busy one, a warning offering Fork instead and nothing opened until it is chosen; with no Claude Code, a message saying how to set it up and New session disabled; and dates as "this minute", "3 hours ago", "yesterday" or the date.

title: A resumed session shows its saved conversation
when: Reads a saved transcript with prompts, meta and command lines, text, tool calls with and without results, a subagent's line and a broken line; then one longer than the limit.
then: Expects the main thread's prompt, text and tool calls, a tool call with no saved result in error, and the rest skipped; and for the long one, only the last `TRANSCRIPT_LIMIT` items after a notice of how many earlier items the transcript holds.

title: The chat loads the plugin of the Lathe the window runs, and its server runs that Lathe
when: Picks the chat's Lathe for a product with its own Lathe that ships the plugin, one whose Lathe does not, one with none (the app's bundled Lathe) and from source; and starts the repo's plugin launcher with LATHE_CLI on a product with no Lathe installed.
then: Expects the product's own plugin and bin, else the app's plugin with the product's bin, else the app's plugin and its bundled bin, the repo's plugin and CLI from source; and the product read by the Lathe named.

title: The plugin's launcher runs the Lathe LATHE_CLI names
when: Starts the plugin's MCP launcher for a product repo with no Lathe installed and LATHE_CLI naming Lathe's bin, and reads the product.
then: Expects the launcher to exit cleanly and the product read.

title: Each permission mode runs the CLI with its own flags; View only takes every write away
when: Builds the CLI's arguments in each mode, and its environment in View only and out of it; and holds the View only list against the CLI's own tools.
then: Expects Ask's ask rules, Accept reads' allowed reads, `--permission-mode auto` and `bypassPermissions`, and View only's reads with every write tool disallowed and Claude told why; LATHE_VIEW_ONLY=1 only in View only; and every tool of the CLI either read only or disallowed.

title: In View only, Lathe's server lists only the reads and refuses every command
when: Lists the tools with and without View only, and in View only calls a command and a query.
then: Expects the queries and the check marked read only, only they listed in View only, the command refused saying the chat is View only with nothing changed, and the query answered.

title: A View only session cannot call a command tool
when: Starts the real plugin launcher with the environment a View only chat gives it, lists its tools and calls a command.
then: Expects no command listed, the call refused saying the chat is View only, and the data unchanged.

title: The mode changes on the open session, and the panel answers prompts by it
when: Drives a ChatSession against a stand-in CLI: starts it View only, changes the mode after a turn and during one, and in View only, Accept reads and Ask has Claude ask for a write and a Lathe query.
then: Expects the plugin loaded and the View only tools counted; the CLI started again on the same session in the new mode, the log saying so, and the change refused while a turn runs; the write refused in View only, saying why; the query run without asking in Accept reads, and asked for in Ask.

title: A folder's chat starts in the mode its last chat had
when: Chooses modes for folders through the Window chat's repository, with and without an open session, and reads them back in a new repository.
then: Expects Accept reads at first, the mode kept by folder (the default left out) and read back, the open session's own mode changed, and refusals while a turn runs and for an unknown mode.

title: The panel answers a prompt by the mode before asking the Owner
when: Decides prompts for Lathe queries and commands and Claude Code's tools in each mode.
then: Expects reads allowed in Accept reads and View only, Ask and Auto asking, Bypass allowing everything, and View only refusing writes even when allowed always.

title: The chat counts the Lathe tools a session gets, or says why they did not load
when: Counts the tools of the repo's plugin on a small product with and without View only, and on a folder with no lathe.config.json.
then: Expects fewer tools in View only, the read-only tools named as Claude Code names them, and the failure saying what is missing.

title: The chat asks the CLI itself whether it is signed in
when: Reads `claude auth status --json` answers, and runs a stand-in CLI that says it is not signed in and exits 1, and one that is missing.
then: Expects signed in, not signed in only with no other way in, unknown otherwise; and the stand-in's answer read, the missing one unknown.

title: A tool allowed always is not asked about again
when: Decides a prompt for a tool allowed always in each mode, and for another tool.
then: Expects the tool allowed in Ask, Accept reads and Auto, and the other tool still asked about.

title: Allow always in this chat: one approval per tool
when: Has the stand-in CLI ask for Bash twice in one turn and answers the first prompt Allow always.
then: Expects one prompt, answered always, and both commands run.

title: A prompt offers Allow always in this chat
when: Pushes a pending prompt and presses Allow always in this chat, then pushes it answered.
then: Expects always sent to the shell and "Allowed always in this chat" shown.

title: Each message carries what the Owner is looking at, as context of its own
when: Writes a message with a focus, a slash command with one, and reads the saved prompt back; reads what Claude is told.
then: Expects the focus as a <lathe-focus> block before the message, none with a slash command, the saved prompt showing only the message, and Claude told to start from the focus and never search the code for the window.

title: Under the desktop chat, Lathe's server tells Claude to use the app tools for the window
when: Starts the server with an app bridge and without, and lists its tools.
then: Expects the instructions to say to use app_focus and app_open, never a search of the code, only with the bridge, and app_focus marked read only.

title: A message goes with what the Owner is looking at
when: Sends a message with a focus to the stand-in CLI.
then: Expects the chat to show only the message, and Claude to answer from the focus with no tool call.

title: The chat knows where the Owner is: a chip above the message box, sent as context
when: Opens a use case on the Graph, sends a message, removes the chip and sends another; and builds the chip at the products.
then: Expects "Viewing DM-SHOP-UC01 on the Graph", the focused record and stage sent with the first message, none with the second, and "Viewing the products" at the start.

title: Dictation shows the words as they are heard, settles them, and leaves the draft to edit
when: Starts dictating into a draft and feeds the guesses and settled words the shell sends, then stops; and lets 20 seconds of quiet pass; and wakes from waiting, sends with "Lathe, send", goes behind another window, and says scratch that, new line and cancel.
then: Expects the guesses at the draft's end replaced by the settled words, nothing sent until asked, the draft kept when dictation ends by itself or behind another window, and each command acting on the draft.

title: After a turn that writes, its records can be put under review: lit on the stage and walked through with their diffs
when: With a turn that changes a command, starts the review and ends it.
then: Expects the review bar with the turn named, the position and diff shown, Highlight changes on, and the bar gone on Done.

title: A record ID in Claude's reply focuses the stage, and Cmd or Ctrl+click opens it in a new tab
when: Draws a reply naming a record and clicks its ID plainly and with Cmd.
then: Expects the new place opened on Cmd+click, the stage left, and the stage focused on a plain click.

title: The Ask Claude About This chip attaches the pointed-at record, sent as context
when: With the desktop chat faked, presses the key that attaches the focused record, sends a message, and takes a chip out.
then: Expects a chip with the record ID and title, the context of the message naming the record, and the chips gone once it is sent.

title: The record's menu offers Ask Claude About This
when: Builds the native menu of a record and chooses its Ask Claude About This.
then: Expects the item after Open in New Tab, and its action called.

title: The chips say the record and its title, and the context lists each record pointed at
when: Names records with and without an index entry and builds the pointed-at context.
then: Expects the ID and title, the ID alone for an unknown record, and a line per known record.

title: Typing / lists the skills and slash commands with one-line descriptions
when: With skills faked, types a slash, narrows it, picks one with Tab, presses Escape, and types a slash mid-message.
then: Expects the list with descriptions, one match after narrowing, the name written into the box, the list closed on Escape and none mid-message.

title: The "/" list matches a leading slash and a name, by prefix first
when: Asks which drafts open the list and which skills match a query.
then: Expects only a slash and a name to open it, and prefix matches before word matches.

title: Typing / lists the skills and commands of the Owner, the folder, Lathe and the plugins, with one-line descriptions
when: Writes skills, commands and plugins into home, folder and plugin folders and lists them.
then: Expects each source listed once with the folder first, descriptions cut to a sentence, Lathe under its prefix and Claude Code's own last.

title: The model and effort the Owner chooses are the CLI's flags, on the same session
when: With a stand-in CLI, chooses a model and effort, sends again, then tries to choose during a turn.
then: Expects the CLI started again with --model and --effort on the same session, the log saying so, and the choice refused during a turn.

title: The model and effort are passed to the CLI, and nothing when left to Claude Code
when: Builds the CLI arguments with and without a choice.
then: Expects --model and --effort only when chosen.

title: The header's picker chooses the model and effort
when: With the desktop chat faked, opens the picker, chooses a model, and lets a turn run.
then: Expects the choice sent, named on the button, and the button disabled while Claude works.

title: The chat's commands take only what the page may send, and only in a window with a session
when: Sends a message and chooses a model in a window with no session, then with one, with good and bad input.
then: Only good input in a window with a session reaches the session: text with pictures it takes, a model and effort Lathe knows.

title: A message typed while Claude works is queued and sent in order
when: With a slow stand-in CLI, sends two messages during a turn and takes one back out.
then: Expects the queue listed in order, one removed, and the other sent when the turn ends.

title: A message typed while Claude works is queued, listed and sent in order; Stop is there while it works
when: With the desktop chat faked, sends during a turn and removes a queued message.
then: Expects Stop shown, the message sent to the shell, the queue listed, and the removal asked.

title: Images are pasted into a message, or the stage is sent as one
when: Pastes an image, sends the stage, sends the message, and pastes an SVG.
then: Expects two thumbnails, both sent with the message and cleared, and the SVG refused.

title: Images go before the text, and files that are not base64 images of a type the CLI takes are refused
when: Builds a message with an image and checks images of other types, other text and too many.
then: Expects the image block before the text and the bad images refused.

title: Only the image types Claude Code reads are sent
when: Asks which types are images the chat sends.
then: Expects PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP only.

title: The shell captures the rectangle of the window the page names, as a PNG, and nothing else
when: Checks rectangles that are good, not finite, empty, too large or not numbers, and captures through a stand-in window.
then: Expects a rounded rectangle, the others refused, the picture as base64 and nothing for a blank capture.

title: Serve serves the app, its reads and change events for the product repo
when: Starts `serve` on port 5340 for a copy of a fixture, using the built app (the package's `dist/app`, or else a build into a temporary folder).
then: Expects the app page and its built script, the same page at client-side routes, the meta model, the product's record summaries and problems read from the engine, a `spec:changed` event on `/api/events` after a data file changes, naming its table and the record summaries but not the meta model, and the next read of the record summaries showing the change, and a POST to an aggregate's command, such as `/api/use-case/change-use-case`, answered with `ok` and the `use_case` table, its change in the file.
