title: A server stopped while a reload is in progress closes the database, and its process exits cleanly
when: In a child process, runs seven rounds, each in a worker thread: starts `serve()` for a small product, loads it, touches a data file and asks for the specs again (a reload), waits 0, 5, 10, 20, 40 or 80 ms, or in the last round until the reload has answered, awaits `stop()` and ends the thread. then: Expects every round and the child process to exit with code 0 and no output on stderr (no "uncaught exception of type Napi::Error"), the first round to have stopped while its reload was in progress, and the last after it had finished.

title: The API serves every product of the workspace, writes to each product's folder and watches each
when: Calls the API for a workspace of two products: each product's record summaries, a write adding a capability under the shop's domain, a write adding a new product, and reads the watched folders.
then: Expects each product's records read from its own folder, the capability written to the shop's data folder only, the new product in the workspace's `data/product.jsonl`, and both data folders watched.

title: A read of the whole workspace joins every product's schema and refuses one product in two folders
when: Reads the meta model and each product's coverage for a workspace whose shop declares its own kind, then lists the products of a workspace whose two folders both hold the same product.
then: Expects the shop's kind in the meta model with its columns, each product's own coverage, and the list refused, naming the product and its two folders.

title: lathe serve listens on this machine alone unless asked for the network, and lists its addresses
when: Lists the network addresses for port 5346 of a machine with loopback, IPv6 and two IPv4 interfaces and of one with loopback alone, then starts serve() for an empty product by default and on every interface, and reads its page on loopback and on this machine's first network address, if it has one.
then: Expects http://192.168.1.20:5346 and http://10.0.0.5:5346 in that order and none for loopback, IPv6 or no network; the default server on 127.0.0.1 and the network one on 0.0.0.0, answering its page on each address.

title: A write from this machine passes the guard; one from another device is refused and marked read-only
when: Sends API writes whose socket comes from 127.0.0.1, ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1, and every write route (a command, snapshot, undo, turn changes) from 192.168.1.20.
then: Expects the loopback writes past the guard (refused only for their body, 415) with no read-only mark, and each write from 192.168.1.20 refused with 403, the reason that changes come only from the machine Lathe runs on, and the read-only mark.

title: A person binds, removes and resets keys, and the keymap follows at once
when: Binds a second key to a shortcut, changes one in place, resets it, rebinds a walk key and a stage key, then resets all.
then: Expects the keymap to follow each change at once, and Reset all to give every shortcut its own keys again.

title: File › Open Records In offers the editors, checks the one in use and chooses another
when: Builds the File menu and chooses another editor in Open Records In.
then: Expects Cursor, Zed, the default app and a command of the Owner's own offered, the one in use checked, and the choice saved.

title: A record's facts offer Reveal, Open in editor and Copy ID in a Product window, and nothing in a browser
when: Opens a record in a Product window, then in a browser.
then: Expects Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in the record's facts in the window, each sending only the ID, and none in the browser.

title: The voice grammar: a pause before the wake phrase wakes, a pause, the wake phrase and a command word is a command, anything else is text
when: Reads words with their times and pauses: the wake phrase after a pause and mid-sentence, as the recognizer writes it, each command after a pause, without one and with more words after it, and the stricter "Hey Lathe".
then: Expects a wake only after a pause, a command only after a pause and ending the utterance, every other word kept as text, and the draft written with capitals, the last sentence scratched and a new paragraph.

title: The chat listens only while its window is in front, and only when the Owner asked
when: Drives a window's listening with a stand-in speech helper: asks to listen behind another window, comes in front, goes behind, comes back, stops; and lets the helper fail.
then: Expects the helper started only while wanted and in front, stopped behind with "background" said to the page and nothing it says after reaching it, and a failure said with its reason.

title: Quick mode sends after the pause end-of-turn detection judges: short when finished, long mid-thought, between when unsure
when: With a fake clock, dictates "zoom into this" with a falling voice, "zoom into the", a rising question, then a sound and a key during the countdown, and dictates without voice detection.
then: Expects sending after 0.5 s, 3.5 s and 2 s, nothing sent once a sound or key cancels, a fixed 2 s without detection, and "Lathe, send" sending at once.

title: A turn is undone in one click through the server, which refuses with its reasons what something since depends on
when: With the server faked, undoes a turn and then a turn the server refuses.
then: Expects the snapshot and the touched records sent, Undone shown, and on refusal the reasons shown with the turn still undoable.

title: Undo names the records Claude's Lathe commands touched, in the order it ran them
when: Takes the IDs from a turn's tool calls, with failed, other and clipped ones among them.
then: Expects the finished Lathe commands' IDs in order and no other.

title: Undoing a turn puts back what it removed, changes back what it changed and removes what it added, in one write
when: On a store, adds, changes and removes outcomes, plans the undo from the rows before and runs it; asks for a kind with no command; adds back a record whose test is gone.
then: Expects the rows as before, the plan in last-command-first order, the unsupported kind named, and a refusal changing nothing.

title: Clear empties Open Recent and the Dock menu
manual_reason: It takes the built app's menus and the Dock: a person checks it.
when: Open two folders, clear File › Open Recent, then open a third.
then: Open Recent and the Dock menu list nothing after Clear, then only the third folder.

title: Claude asks what the Reader is looking at and opens a record, only with an app window connected
when: Lists the MCP server's tools with and without an app bridge, reads the bridge from the environment, and calls `app_focus` and `app_open` through a stand-in bridge, then with none, a closed window, an unreachable bridge and a wrong token.
then: Expects `app_focus` and `app_open` listed only with a bridge; the bridge read only for a local address with its token; the focus named by ID, kind, title and stage with the product and page; a record opened, a refusal passed on as an error and a bad stage refused; and "No Lathe app window is connected" in every other case.

title: The app bridge answers for its window, and only with its token
when: Starts the app bridge and calls a window's focus and open routes with and without its token, a closed window's and an unknown route, and checks open requests.
then: Expects a 127.0.0.1 address per window with a 48-hex-digit token; the window's focus, and 404 for a closed window; the record opened with the window's answer passed on, a bad ID 400; 401 for a wrong token, 405 for a GET to open and 404 for another route; and an open request with an ID and a known stage or none accepted, others refused.

title: The page answers the app bridge: what the Reader is looking at, and opening a record
when: Opens a use case on the ERD stage and answers the bridge's focus question, then opens a command on the Graph stage and a record that does not exist.
then: Expects the focus named by ID, kind and title with its stage and product; the command opened at its address with a message naming it and the stage; and a refusal saying there is no such record in this window's specs.

title: lathe app focus and lathe app open reach the window as the app tools do, and refuse with none
when: Runs lathe app focus and lathe app open against a stand-in bridge, against a closed window and with none.
then: Expects the text and JSON app_focus and app_open give, the record opened on the stage given, a refusal with exit 1 when no window is connected, and exit 2 for bad usage.

title: The sign-in runs Claude Code's own login, passes on its link and code, and asks again when it ends
when: Runs a sign-in of a stand-in `claude` that prints the sign-in page's link and then signs in, asks for a code, or fails; gives it a code of two lines and then the good one; and has a stand-in that ends well but still says it is not signed in.
then: Expects `auth login` run with `--claudeai` or `--console` only, a second start refused; the link read through the CLI's colors (an http link never), the code asked for, refused on two lines and written once; signed in once `auth status` says so; and the CLI's last line, or that it is still not signed in, as the failure, with a new start allowed.

title: The sign-in commands reach the sign-in under way through the repository
when: With no sign-in, gives a code and cancels; starts one with no agent found; then starts one, gives a code that is not text and one that is, cancels it, and signs out with no agent found.
then: Expects the code and the cancel refused with none running and the start refused with no agent; the sign-in started with its way in, the text code alone passed on, the cancel passed on, and the sign-out refused.

title: A turn that finds Claude Code not signed in marks the chat signed out, not Claude's answer
when: Reads the lines the CLI prints when it is not signed in (its synthetic message marked authentication_failed and its result), the same words unmarked, an invalid key's result, and a long answer that only mentions /login.
then: Expects the chat idle and marked signed out with neither line shown, the mark sent in the page's patch, each other form of the words marked too, and the long answer kept as Claude's answer.

title: The chat ends Claude Code when a turn finds it not signed in, and the next message starts it again
when: Drives a ChatSession against a stand-in CLI that answers a message as the real one does when it is not signed in, then sends another message.
then: Expects the chat closed and marked signed out with only the Owner's message in it and no CLI running; the next message clears the mark, starts the CLI again and gets an answer.

title: Cancel stops the sign-in under way, and nothing changes
when: Starts a sign-in of a stand-in `claude` that waits for the browser, cancels it once it has printed the link, then cancels again and gives a code.
then: Expects the CLI stopped, no sign-in under way and the stand-in still signed out; the second cancel and the code refused.

title: Signing out runs Claude Code's own logout
when: Signs a stand-in `claude` in, then signs it out, and signs out a `claude` that does not exist.
then: Expects `auth status` to say signed in, then not signed in after `auth logout`, and the missing one's sign-out refused.

title: The migrations are numbered in order and recorded as applied
when: Applies the migrations to a fresh database.
then: Expects them numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, each recorded with its name.

title: The schema read back loads each stored table after the tables it points at
when: Reads the schema's load order and foreign keys.
then: Expects every stored table a foreign key points at to come before it.

title: Removing a product kind while a record of it is left is refused
when: Opens a store whose product declares the kind `memo` under a domain and holds the record EX-LEND-M01 of it, then removes the `memo` product kind.
then: Expects the removal refused, naming `memo`.

title: The row types in src/store/tables.ts match the schema
when: Renders the row types from the schema description.
then: Expects them to equal the committed `lathe/src/platform/data/tables.ts`.

title: Every kind has an ID in the registry, a title and its parent columns
when: Reads every kind's table and parents from the schema description.
then: Expects each kind's table keyed by `id`, with a foreign key from `id` into `record_id`, a required title and a foreign key for each parent column; a lone parent column required, and two or three parent columns all optional with a CHECK that exactly one is given.

title: Each relation's pairs fit its link table's ends
when: Reads every relation's pairs and every supertype's members from the schema description.
then: Expects every relation to have pairs, each pair's kinds accepted by the link table's ends or their supertypes, and every supertype member a kind.

title: The server has no way to change the meta-model
when: Sends POST and PUT requests to the meta model's read, `/api/meta-model/get-meta-model`, and to schema-like paths, and a write to a meta table, on the running server.
then: Expects them refused, and the migrations unchanged.

title: Which kinds are obligations, and which links design or prove a product's own obligation, come from the schema
when: Loads a product with its own obligation kind, with a design relation, a proof relation and one with no role.
then: Coverage lists exactly the kinds flagged as obligations; a record reached by the design and proof relations is designed and proved, one reached only by the relation with no role is neither.

title: Each kind the schema flags as an obligation is a member of the obligation supertype, and only those
when: Reads the schema's kinds and supertypes.
then: Expects the obligation supertype to be exactly Lathe's ten obligation kinds.

title: The schema describes every table and every column of a stored table
when: Reads every table and column in the schema description.
then: Expects a description on every table, and on every column of a stored table that is not a link table.

title: The schema version is one whole number in schema/version.json, and each converter moves the data forward one version
when: Reads schema/version.json and Lathe's own converters, then a folder of converters with one that skips a version.
then: Expects SCHEMA_VERSION to be the file's number, Lathe's converters to chain from 1 to it one version each, and a converter that skips a version refused.

title: 1-to-2 puts every flow through its product's one new interface, renaming its flows, steps and tests wherever they are named
when: Runs every converter from 1 on a committed product at schema 1 with a flow, its step and test, a fulfills link and a requirement whose text names the step.
then: Every ID and mention ends in FL01 after 1-to-2, the flow going through the new TL-IF01, internal; 3-to-4 then merges it back into the use case's one flow, offered through TL-IF01; the data is at this Lathe's schema, and the to-dos say what is left.

title: 1-to-2 gives every test one of the five levels, and a manual test the level that fits its kind
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of each test kind at the seven old levels, manual among them.
then: database becomes integration, api and contract service, e2e-api system, e2e-ui browser; a manual flow, view, use case or policy test browser, any other the lowest level its kind allows, with a to-do to check it.

title: 1-to-2 puts every repository under its aggregate's domain, persisting that aggregate, renamed wherever it is named
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of repositories under their aggregates, in two domains, one named by a link, a part and a text.
then: Each repository sits under its aggregate's domain as <domain>-REPO<nn>, numbered in its aggregates' order, with a persists link to its one aggregate; the link, the part and the text name the new ID, and the to-dos say to split a class that persists several aggregates into one repository each, and to rename the IDs in code.

title: 1-to-2 drops the descriptions that are gone, opens each When with its Given, and stands in for each required text a record lacks
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of two commands (one without a description), a data model with a description, a flow step, and two invariant tests with a Given, one without a When.
then: Expects the data model's description gone and the step with none, each Given opening its test's When (or becoming it), the command without a description given "To write: what it changes and when it is refused.", the three changes counted, and one to-do naming TL-LEND-CMD02's description.

title: 1-to-2 puts each command under its aggregate's root entity, and leaves a to-do for an aggregate with none
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on a command of an aggregate with a root entity and one of an aggregate with none.
then: Expects the first under the root entity (entity_id in place of aggregate_id), the second left as it was with a to-do naming it, and the to-do to move commands that change a child entity.

title: 1-to-2 drops every recorded exception and waiver, and leaves a to-do to change the model
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of a command change, a repository share, a pattern rule with its setting and applies-when condition, and a setting value with a not-applicable reason.
then: The command change and the repository share are gone, the rule keeps only its own columns, the reason is the setting's value, and the to-dos name each one to change in the model.

title: 2-to-3 gives each check the domain of its check_row record, removes the check_row records and kind, and leaves a to-do for a check no record names
when: Runs the 2-to-3 converter's files phase on raw rows of two checks, one check_row record naming the first, and the check_row kind with its fields.
then: The first check has its domain_id, the check_row records, kind and fields are gone, and the to-do names the second check and the fix.

title: 2-to-3 leaves a to-do for every check of a product with no check_row records
when: Runs the 2-to-3 converter's files phase on raw rows of one check and no check_row records.
then: The check is unchanged, nothing is reported as changed, and the to-do names the check.

title: 2-to-3 does nothing to data that is already upgraded
when: Runs the 2-to-3 converter's files phase on a check that has its domain_id.
then: No table changes and there are no changes or to-dos.

title: 3-to-4 gives each product kind its complexity from its stage, makes each standard engineering with a to-do to review it, gives each product setting no technology words, and makes each interface internal with a to-do to mark the public ones
when: Runs the 3-to-4 converter's files phase on product kinds of the technical specification, the test plan, interface design and no stage, a standard with no type, a product setting with no technology words and an interface that says nothing of being public.
then: Each product kind is accidental, as-parent, essential and essential; the standard is engineering with a to-do naming it to review as a quality; the setting lists no words; the interface is internal with a to-do naming it to mark public where it is; four changes are reported.

title: 3-to-4 does nothing to data that is already upgraded
when: Runs the 3-to-4 converter's files phase on a product kind with its complexity, a standard with its type, a setting with its technology words and a public interface.
then: No table changes and there are no changes or to-dos.

title: 3-to-4 drops a product's declaration of a provided_by, fills or generates pair its own kind now has, as Lathe's kinds have them, and keeps every other
when: Runs the 3-to-4 converter's files phase on an accidental kind and an obligation kind whose product declares their fills, generates and provided_by pairs, beside a provided_by pair with the product's kind as provider and another relation.
then: Only the declarations of the pairs the kinds now have are dropped, with one change naming each.

title: 3-to-4 merges a use case's flows into one, keeping the union of their steps, marking variants, and reports what it cannot merge
when: Runs 3-to-4 on a use case with a web app flow and a CLI flow, each with a step invoking the same command, one step of its own each, a view the web steps happen in, and a test each.
then: Expects one flow titled as the use case; the shared step once with both requirements; each flow's own step a variant of its interface; the view presenting the command; both interfaces offering the use case; the automated system test kept as the flow's, the other gone and what named it renamed; and to-dos for the gone test, the variants, the step whose view is lost and the interfaces' roles.

title: 4-to-5 changes no row, asks to rename a product's own kind or relation that clashes with a new table, and to write the journey each duration outcome times
when: Runs the 4-to-5 converter's files phase on a product kind named journey, two pairs of a product relation named carries_out beside another relation, and three outcomes whose measures are a share, a median of days from one moment to another, and how long something takes.
then: No table changes and no changes are reported; one to-do names the kind and the relation once to rename, and one names the two duration outcomes to write journeys for.

title: 4-to-5 tells a product with no journeys where they go, and says nothing to one that has them
when: Runs the 4-to-5 converter's files phase on a product with one outcome and no journeys, then on the same product with a journey.
then: The first gets one to-do saying journeys arrive in Discovery; the second no table changes, no changes and no to-dos.

title: 5-to-6 numbers each product's domains from 1 in ID order, the numbers inside IDs compared by value, and changes nothing else
when: Runs the 5-to-6 converter's files phase on domains of two products, one with IDs XX-D2 and XX-D10, then on data with no domains.
then: Each domain gains position after product_id, numbered from 1 within its product (D2 before D10); other tables are unchanged; the first run reports one change, the second none.

title: 6-to-7 moves each product kind in interaction-design to interface-design, keeps its other fields and every other kind, and does nothing to data already upgraded
when: Runs the 6-to-7 converter's files phase on a product kind in interaction-design and one in technical-specification, then again on the converted data.
then: The first kind is in interface-design with its other fields as they were, the second unchanged, one change reported naming the kind and no to-dos; the second run changes nothing and reports nothing.

title: Each test is of the test kind named after what it tests, and sits under that one record, which it proves
when: A use case test is removed, or written under another requirement.
then: Each test kind has one required parent named by its kind; only that requirement goes unproved.

title: A declared product kind and its record load on the next load, placed under its domain
when: Loads a product that declares the kind `memo` under a domain, at stage `use-cases`, with its record EX-LEND-M01 under EX-LEND.
then: Expects `memo` listed last with stage `use-cases`, no position and parent kind `domain`, EX-LEND-M01 placed under EX-LEND in domain EX-LEND, and no problems.

title: A product kind and relation are declared, changed and removed through the Product aggregate
when: Declares a product kind with its fields and a relation, adds a record of the kind, changes the fields, then removes the kind with records and without.
then: Expects the kind's table to follow each declaration, and a kind still holding records to be refused at the commit.

title: A product's own kind is listed after Lathe's, with its own label, stage and obligation, and Lathe's kinds keep theirs
when: Loads a product with its own kind in the domain model.
then: The product's kind comes after Lathe's, with its own label, stage, parent and obligation; Lathe's kinds are as in a product with no kinds of its own.

title: A product relation with a new name gets a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name adds only its pair
when: Loads a product that declares a pair for Lathe's `about` and a relation of its own.
then: `about` gains only the new pair and Lathe's other relations are unchanged; the product's relation gets its own link table.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line and the line of the first
when: The same product kind is declared twice.
then: A primary-key refusal on line 2 of the declaration file, naming the kind and line 1.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused once
when: Loads a product relation written twice in its file.
then: Expects one primary-key refusal naming data/product_relation.jsonl, line 2.

title: A product's interface design kind may present commands and queries; any other kind may not
when: Loads a product that declares an interface design kind under its domain with presents pairs to command and query, and links one of its records to a command and a query of the domain; then declares presents from a kind of another stage.
then: The link loads and the record lists both as Presents, each command or query lists it as Presented in; the pair from the other stage is refused as product-relation-own.

title: The engine loads the six stages in order and each kind's stage and position, with the product and open questions outside them
when: A product is loaded.
then: Expects six stages in order, from Discovery to Test plan, each described; kind positions 1, 2, 3 running stage by stage; and only the product and the open question with no stage.

title: Every kind's stage is one of the schema's stages, and a product kind with no stage sits in none
when: Loads a product kind with no stage.
then: Every kind's stage is one of the schema's; the product kind has no stage and no position; the stages are unchanged.

title: The schema orders the stages, and the kinds stage by stage with the product first and open questions last
when: Reads the schema's stages and kinds.
then: Expects the six stages in order, and kind positions 1, 2, 3 running stage by stage from the product to the open question.

title: A product places its own kind in one of the six stages, or none, and cannot add a stage or change one of Lathe's kinds
when: Declares a product kind in each of the six stages, in none, in a stage that does not exist, and with the name of one of Lathe's kinds.
then: Each stage and no stage load and the stages are unchanged; the unknown stage and Lathe's name are refused.

title: Reads kinds, folders and relations from the schema, kinds in the schema's order
when: Builds the app's workspace from a product's schema description.
then: Expects kinds in the schema's kind positions, from product, business outcome and domain to question; the UC requirement's label, stage, parent, obligation, ID scope and required `statement`; the endpoint's two parents and the view's none; the six stages in order; and the `fulfills` relation with its design role and label.

title: The meta model read gives the kinds in the schema's reading order, the stages, the relations' words and each table's columns
when: Reads get-meta-model over two products' data.
then: Expects the product first and kinds by position, each with its stage, parents and ID scope; the six stages in order; each relation pair with its words from both ends; and every non-link table's columns.

title: The Markdown gives the data model, then kinds with their tables, other tables, relations, folders and checks, each with an anchor
when: Renders Lathe's reference as Markdown.
then: Expects `# Lathe reference` first, then the data files, each stage from Domain model to Test plan with its kinds, checks and coverage gaps, Outside the stages with the open question, then Other tables, Relations and Checks of any kind; anchors for a stage, a kind, a table, a part table, a relation, a check and a gap; and more than 100 links inside the document, each landing on an anchor.

title: The reference script prints a product's reference, or writes it with --out
when: Runs the reference script for a product with its own kinds, with `--print` and with `--out`.
then: Expects the rendered reference in both.

title: The reference holds every kind, table, relation, folder and check of Lathe's schema
when: Builds Lathe's reference.
then: Expects the six stages in order, a use case's label, stage, parent, ID scope, ID pattern and children, the ten obligation kinds with their coverage and test kinds with their levels, each kind's table with its columns and references, a part table, a relation's pairs and role, every check row in run order, the engine's own `data-refused` and every gap rule.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and relations and its own checks
when: Builds the reference for a product with its own kind, relation and checks.
then: Expects a product's own kind with its table and relation pair, and its own checks after Lathe's.

title: The committed REFERENCE.md is the reference as the reference script writes it
when: Renders Lathe's reference.
then: Expects it to equal the committed `lathe/REFERENCE.md`.

title: A product's own checks are held to the same rule, and Lathe's are all documented
when: Reads Lathe's reference, and the reference of a product with checks of its own.
then: Expects every kind, table and check of Lathe's described, and a product's own checks with their summary and explanation.

title: The reference reads each relation by its labels
when: Builds the default reference.
then: Expects `fulfills` to carry the labels Fulfills and Fulfilled by, the relation's entry to read `Reads: Fulfills / Fulfilled by`, and the UC requirement's entry to list `Fulfilled by` under Links in.

title: A kind and a check open from where the Reader meets them
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reading a record opens its kind, a column and a problem code and lands on the format page each time, without leaving the workbench.
when: Open a record's page; choose its kind in the wiki card, a column's label, and a problem's code.
then: Each opens its kind or check page in the same workbench, one step each.

title: The merge keeps the rows both sides added, sorted
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects both sides' new rows in the merged file, sorted by key.

title: The merge takes a change or a removal made on one side only
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects the one side's change and removal in the merged file.

title: The merge keeps one copy of a row both sides added alike, and of a link both sides made
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects each row once.

title: A field the other side added survives the merge
when: Merges a view file where the other side added a field this side's schema does not know.
then: Expects the merged row to keep the field, the rows sorted, no clash and no problem, the table's check left to the next load.

title: One side's removals and change survive while another row clashes
when: Merges a view file, by itself and through git with the driver set up, where one side removed two rows and changed one, and the other left them alone, added a row and added a key the first side also added with other content.
then: Expects the rows to stay removed, the change kept, the new row added and the key both sides added reported as a clash between conflict markers, with either side as ours.

title: lathe merge-data exits 1 with the clash on a real clash, and 0 on a clean merge
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects exit 1 naming the clash, and 0 for a clean merge.

title: The merge checks the merged table's own rules
when: Merges flow steps where each side adds a step at position 2 of the same path, an invariant test whose state is `done`, and table keys each side added at another position.
then: Expects the steps to merge with no clash but the problem 'the merged flow_step breaks a rule of its table', the test refused with 'invariant_test.state "done" is not one of automated, manual, not automated yet', and the table keys merged by table and position, sorted, with no clash or problem.

title: lathe merge-data writes the merge over ours, as git expects
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects the merged file written over ours.

title: A driver whose lathe is not installed fails the merge loudly
when: Merges two branches through git with the driver run from a copy of the command line that has no packages installed.
then: Expects the merge to stop with the file conflicted and holding our side, and a message naming the missing package, saying the file was not merged, and giving npm ci and git checkout -m.

title: A business outcome sits under its product and gives a statement, its measure and its target
when: Loads a business outcome without its statement, measure or target, one with a blank one, and one whose ID names another product.
then: Each missing column is required, a blank one is refused, the ID must start with its product's, and the kind sits in discovery under the product.

title: Each Business outcome command changes one outcome through its repository
when: Adds and changes business outcomes with what measures them, and gives an outcome of no product, a taken ID and inputs of another shape.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the outcome's tables, and each refused one to name its reason and change no file.

title: A business outcome goes with its measured_by links, refused while a capability serves it
when: Removes an outcome with its measured_by link, then one a capability serves.
then: Expects the first to go with its link, and the second to be refused, naming the capability.

title: The CLI, the MCP tools and HTTP each run the Business outcome command they name
when: Runs Business outcome commands and queries as lathe business-outcome, as MCP tools and as POST /api/business-outcome/<command>.
then: Expects each to run the one command it names, and a refusal to answer 422.

title: Discovery is the first stage, before the domain model, and its kinds are the business outcome and the journey
when: Reads the stages and the kinds' order from the schema description.
then: The stages start with discovery, its kinds are the business outcome, the journey and the journey step, and they follow the product in the kinds' order.

title: An outcome is measured by tests of any kind, or by records of the product's own kinds it allows, or says how it is measured outside the code
when: Links an outcome to two tests, to a use case, and to a CLI command before and after the product allows that kind; links a use case to a test, and an outcome to another product's test; gives a measure outside the code, and a blank one.
then: The tests and the allowed record load; the use case and the record not yet allowed are refused by relation-pair, a use case as the source by its foreign key, the other product's test by link-crosses-product, and the blank text as a column.

title: Each Interface command changes one interface through its repository
when: Runs each Interface command on a store built from the data set: adds and changes an interface with the roles that use it and the use cases it offers, reads it through its product, and gives inputs of another shape, an ID in use and a product or interface that is not there.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the Interface aggregate's tables, the product to read the interface with its offers by capability, and each refused one to name its rule and reason.

title: An interface goes with its roles and offers, refused while referenced
when: Removes an interface a flow step is a variant of, then one with roles and offers that nothing references.
then: Expects the referenced one to be refused, naming the step, and the other to go with its roles and the use cases it offers.

title: The CLI, the MCP tools and HTTP each run the Interface command they name
when: Runs the Interface commands as lathe interface with flags and JSON, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/interface/<command>.
then: Expects each to run the one command it names, a refusal to give every reason, and a wrong input to be refused before anything is read.

title: A journey without its trigger or its result, or under another product, is refused
when: Adds a journey without its trigger, one with a blank result, and one whose ID names another product.
then: Expects each refused with every reason, and a journey with both added under its product.

title: A step carries out a use case of another domain, a policy, or nothing yet, and never a record of another product
when: Adds steps carrying out a use case of each of two domains, a policy, and nothing, then a use case of another product and a command.
then: Expects the first four added and the last two refused, naming the step.

title: Moving a step keeps every path of its journey numbered 1, 2, 3
when: Moves the last step of the main path first, then moves a step from the main path onto an alternate path.
then: Expects each path numbered 1, 2, 3 after each move, the steps in their new order, and a second step at a taken position refused.

title: A journey path whose positions skip a number is a step-order error
when: Loads the complete product with its journey, then with the journey's third main step at position 5.
then: Expects no step-order error, then one on that step, naming positions 3 and 4 as missing.

title: A journey serves its product's outcomes, and what its steps carry out serves them through it
when: Links a journey to two outcomes of its product and one of another product, then reads what a use case one of its steps carries out serves.
then: Expects the other product's outcome refused with nothing written, and the use case and the handoff's policy to serve both outcomes through the journey.

title: A journey serves its outcomes, and the pages of its use case, its policy and its outcome name it
when: Sets a journey to serve an outcome of its product, with a step carrying out a use case and another a policy, then reads the use case, the policy's command and the outcome.
then: Expects the use case and the policy to name the journey with their step, path, position and the steps before and after, the outcome to list the journey beside its capability, and the journey page to say what each step carries out.

title: A second journey test of a journey is refused
when: Adds a journey test to a journey, then a second.
then: Expects the first added with its ID the journey's and T, and the second refused.

title: A journey test proves only at the service, system or browser level
when: Loads the complete product with its journey whose journey test runs at the unit level.
then: Expects a test-level-not-allowed warning on the journey test, the levels allowed being service, system and browser.

title: Removing a use case a step carries out is refused naming the step, and removing the journey keeps it

title: A test case naming no test whose file it is in is an error; one named in its describe or each rows is not

title: A file a test names is read for test cases, whatever its name

title: A product's trace rows read gives each use case once, from its outcomes to its acceptance tests, with its status per stage

then: Expects each use case once with its outcomes, requirements, what it changes and reads, its flow's steps with their design and technical chain, its flow test, what its tests rest on and its status per stage; a requirement no step designs and one not proved counted; and an unknown product or data without the run refused.

title: The Reader reads coverage for every obligation kind and every test state

then: What the requirement says is on the page.

manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.

then: What the requirement says is on the page.

title: The record trace read gives an obligation's chain, its built marks and its standing where it is owed

title: The record trace read judges each of a use case's requirements in its domain

title: The record trace read gives a technical record the obligations it builds, with their tests and states
when: Reads get-record-trace for a rule whose chain builds an invariant proved by an automated test, and for the test.

title: The record trace read gives a test what it proves and its run by, and a test data set none
when: Reads get-record-trace for a test and for a test data set.
then: Expects the test's parent as what it proves and its level, state, file, size and markers; a test data set has no run by.

title: An endpoint handler's file that does not name its method and route is an error
when: Loads endpoints whose handlers' files name the route with its method, with another method, with the method too far away, as a regular expression, not at all, or are missing.
then: Expects an endpoint-route-not-in-file error for the other method, the far method and the unnamed route, naming the endpoint, route and file, and none for the rest.

title: A view whose route no component file names is an error
when: Loads views rendered by components whose files name the route another way, do not name it, or are missing, and a view with no route.
then: Expects a view-route-not-in-file error only for the view whose component file does not name its route.

title: A route the code serves with no endpoint or view is a gap
when: Loads a product whose handler file and router file serve routes by method calls, keys, comparisons and route constants, some with records and some without, and others only in comments.
then: Expects route-without-record gaps of the product for `/health`, `/tools/:id` and `DELETE /loans/:id`, each naming its file and line, and none for the commented route or `/catalog`; no router files by default and a `routers` that is not a list refused; and the recognizer reading `GET /a`, `/` and `/c/{}` but not a commented route or a plain string.

title: The addresses traced both ways read lists the product's addresses its files do not name and those its code serves with no record
when: Reads list-traced-addresses for each of two products over a checks' run holding address problems, a route-without-record gap and other problems.
then: Expects each product's own address problems and served addresses with no record, nothing else, and a refusal for no such product.

title: A table's file that lacks its name, a column or a key is a warning for each
when: Loads a product whose tables name a SQL file that defines one table whole, leaves out another's column and keys, and defines no third; and a view whose file selects its columns.
then: Expects table-schema-mismatch warnings for `member_id`, the primary key and the foreign key of `loans` and for no table `tools`; none once the file is written whole, apart from a foreign key to the wrong table; and with the file missing, technical-file-missing on all three tables and no table-schema-mismatch.

title: A table kept in a database whose file leaves out a column is a table-schema-mismatch warning
when: Loads the complete product with a schema file whose tables lack their columns.
then: Expects table-schema-mismatch warnings for each table it names, and only those.

title: The stored kinds not defined read lists the product's table-schema-mismatch warnings alone
when: Reads find-undefined-stored-kinds for one of two products over a checks' run holding table-schema-mismatch and other problems.
then: Expects only its own product's table-schema-mismatch warnings, and a refusal for no such product.

title: A table's columns come from column names, field names, flattened value objects and children kept in the root's table
when: Gives an entity a field with a column name, one named in words, one typed by a value object of two fields, and a child kept in its root's table.
then: Expects exactly those columns, and the recognizer to read inline and table keys, indexes, ALTER TABLE, quoted names and the names a SELECT list gives with AS.

title: A table stored as a table with no file is a gap; one in browser storage is not
when: Clears a table's file, and keeps another in browser storage with no file.
then: Expects a table-without-file gap on the first only.

title: A package no record names is one gap on the product, until a record names it
when: Loads a product whose two package.json files list four packages across the four sections, one named on its adapter; then names the rest.
then: Expects one gap on the product naming the three others with their manifests, then no gap and no problem.

title: The unused packages read gives the product's one package-not-accounted-for gap, or none
when: Reads find-unused-packages for a product with that gap among others and for one without it, over a checks' run.
then: Expects that gap alone for the first, none for the second.

title: A record naming a package no manifest lists is an error
when: Loads an adapter naming a listed package and an unlisted one; then the same with no package.json at all.
then: Expects one package-not-in-manifest error naming the adapter and the unlisted package, then the adapter reported again.

title: A record naming a package no manifest lists is an error, as Lathe's checks report it
when: Loads the complete product with its adapter naming one package its package.json lists and one it does not.
then: Expects one package-not-in-manifest error, naming the adapter and the unlisted package.

title: Only a technical record names a package, a tooling record included
when: Loads a package on a use case, a name npm does not allow, and a package on a tooling record.
then: Expects package-use-technical and the table's CHECK to refuse the first two, and the tooling record to account for its package.

title: The manifests are the listed folders, or the root and the folders under it
when: Loads manifests at the root, one folder down, two folders down, under node_modules and in a hidden folder; then lists one folder; then a folder with none and one outside the root.
then: Expects the root and the folder directly under it found, only the listed one read, and each config mistake to stop the load naming the folder.

title: get-serves names the outcomes a record serves and the use cases it serves them through
when: Reads get-serves over the complete product for an aggregate, a storage requirement, a view requirement, a domain and an unknown record.
then: Expects each reached record's outcomes and use cases, none for the domain, and a refusal for the unknown record.

title: An aggregate, read model or obligation no outcome reaches is a serves-no-outcome warning saying how to fix it
when: Loads the complete product, then the same with no capability serving an outcome.
then: Expects no warning, then one for each aggregate, read model and obligation, with its message.

title: A read model only an unreached query reads serves no outcome
when: Loads the complete product with no step invoking its query.
then: Expects a serves-no-outcome warning for its read model alone.

title: list-serves lists a product's records by outcome and those no outcome reaches
when: Reads list-serves over the complete product, then with no step invoking its query, then for an unknown product.
then: Expects every reached record with its outcomes and none unserved, then the read model as serving none, then a refusal.

title: Each Slot filling command changes one fill through its repository, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Fills a slot with a hand-written tooling record and stops filling it, tries to fill it with a generated record, twice, with a domain, and stops a fill that is not there, then runs the commands as lathe slot-filling, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/slot-filling/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the fills table, each refused one to name its rule and reason and change nothing, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: Fill slot refuses a standard and a standard rule, and says that the records that meet its rules account for an engineering standard

title: A journey reads as proved only when its journey test and every step are

title: A journey's proof shows with the journey, with its outcome and between the outcomes and use cases of the trace
when: Opens a journey, an outcome it serves and the product's Trace stage.
then: Expects the same proof line in all three, and in the trace a line from the outcome to the journey and from the journey to each use case its steps carry out.

title: Each journey gap is reported with what to write
when: Loads a product with a journey without a test, one with no main path, one serving no outcome, and a step that carries out nothing.
then: Expects journey-without-test, journey-without-main-path, journey-serves-no-outcome and journey-step-unlinked, one each, each saying what to write.

title: Each Provision command changes one record's provider through its repository, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Names a data store's provider, replaces it, names a tooling record's, and removes the data store's; tries a domain, a provider of another kind and a removal of no provider; then runs the commands as lathe provision, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/provision/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the provided_by table with one provider per record, each refused one to name its rule and reason and change nothing, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: The reach of a change lists every record that sits under it or depends on it, each once, by stage, never up to a purpose

then: Expects each record that sits under the change or depends on it once, by stage with the path that reaches it, the technical records its chain says build it, no integration a chain counts as a provider, and no use case, capability or outcome among them.

title: The reach names the code files and the tests a change touches, each test with its state

then: Expects each file with the records naming it, each test with its state and file, and the text naming them.

title: The reach names the use cases, journeys and business outcomes its records serve

then: Expects the command's use cases and outcome, and none for the outcome, which the text says no use case reaches.

title: A change of several records reads as one reach, each record once with the changed records it is reached from

title: Only an automated test needs a file, and only a manual test gives a reason

title: A level outside the five, or none, is refused

title: A test data set sits under a domain, and any kind of test starts from any number of them

title: Each Test data set command changes one test data set through its repository, and one a test starts from stays

title: A data set no test starts from is an error; a missing file is an error when an automated test starts from it, else a warning

then: test-data-set-unused is an error; test-data-set-file-missing is an error, then a warning; a folder gives no problem.

title: Each Pattern command changes one pattern through its repository, its settings given in order

title: A pattern rule is owed by each domain that follows its pattern, itself or through a use case, and proved there by one pattern rule test

then: The rule is owed in both and proved only in the first; a second test for one rule and domain is refused; a test naming a non-follower is an error.

title: A use case has one flow, the same through every interface, whose steps need a path and a position, fulfill its requirements, invoke a command or query, exchange with integrations and may be a variant

title: A well-formed flow raises no step problem; a second flow for the use case, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke are refused

then: No step-order problem on the good flow; each broken row is refused.

title: A UC requirement no step of its flow fulfills is reported as not designed

then: A designed gap and a not-designed warning, for that requirement only.

title: A flow's ID is its use case's ID and FL
when: A flow through a second interface is added with the right ID, a wrong one, and through another product's interface.
then: The first is accepted; flow-id-interface refuses the second and reference-crosses-product the third.

title: Every aggregate's next-id query answers the shape its kind's id_pattern gives

then: Each answer has the record's prefix and at least its digits, and is past the record's number (a flow's is its use case's and FL).

title: A step an offering interface cannot reach is reported, for each kind of interface
when: Makes the complete product's interface an API, with its steps in no view.
then: step-unreached warns of each step whose command or query an offering web app or desktop has no view for, an API no endpoint for, and a CLI or agent tools no record of its own for; a variant of another interface and an interface of kind other are left be.

title: A variant of an interface that does not offer its use case is an error
when: Makes a step a variant of an interface that does not offer its use case.
then: variant-not-offered reports the step as an error, naming the interface and the use case.

title: A use case with a flow no interface offers is warned of
when: Removes every interface's offer of a use case that has a flow.
then: flow-not-offered warns of the use case.

title: An interface that offers a use case none of whose actors is among its roles is warned of
when: Gives an interface roles that are none of an offered use case's actors.
then: interface-actor-not-the-use-case warns of the interface, naming its roles.

title: A command line or agent tools reaches a step through a record of the product's own that presents its command or query, scoped as a view is
when: Gives the complete product a command line that offers a use case and an interface design kind of its own that presents commands and queries, then has one record present the step's command and query, under no interface, under that interface, and under another.
then: step-unreached leaves the steps be while the record presents them and sits under no interface or under that interface, and warns of them when it sits under another interface or presents nothing; the use case read model names the record as where each step is carried out.

title: Each offering interface's version of a flow is derived: where each step is carried out, its actor, the variants left out
when: Reads a use case whose flow a web app and an API offer, with a variant only the web app does.
then: Expects the web app's version to carry the step out in the view that presents its command and to keep its variant, the API's in the endpoint that exposes it without the variant, and each with the first of the use case's actors it lists.

title: An interface that offers no use case is a gap

then: An interface-without-flow gap names it.

title: Each use case command changes one use case through its repository and is refused, changing nothing, when it breaks a rule

then: Expects each accepted command to write only the Use case aggregate's tables, and each refused one to name its rule and reason and leave every data file as it was.

title: Only repositories write data files, a handler loads only its own aggregate, and every command has its definition

then: Expects only repositories to import data-files.ts, only command handlers to import repositories and each only its own aggregate's, and every command of an aggregate with a slice to have its definition.

title: A flow step moves to a position of its path or another, and every path stays numbered 1, 2, 3

then: Expects each path numbered 1, 2, 3 after each move, and the last move refused, changing nothing.

title: A use case goes whole, and a record referenced from outside what goes stays
when: Removes a use case with a requirement, flow and step, then a use case another aggregate follows and asks about, a requirement a step fulfills, a flow with its steps and a test a business outcome is measured by.
then: Expects the first use case and its flow to go with everything under them, and every other removal to be refused, naming each referrer.

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
when: Loads a use case with no flow.
then: Expects a use-case-without-flow gap in its domain, and no error.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group, a column whose renaming changes no ID
when: A group is set on each of the five kinds, then renamed.
then: group_name is optional on all five; no ID changes and the renamed group loads.

title: A use case under a capability, and everything under it, belongs to the capability's domain and counts in its coverage
when: A use case is moved under another capability of its domain.
then: Everything under a capability carries its domain and the pattern none; after the move the domain and the coverage are unchanged.

title: A path whose positions skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap
when: Loads two steps of one flow on one path, written `refused` and `Refused`, at positions 2 and 3 with no step at 1.
then: Expects one `step-order` error, on the step at position 2.

title: A requirement moved to another use case takes its next number, its tests follow, and one a step fulfills stays
when: Moves a requirement no step fulfills to a use case of another domain, then a requirement a step fulfills.
then: Expects the first to take the other use case's next requirement number with its tests renamed and every mention following, and the second refused, naming the step.

title: The same step written per interface is an error
